transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-15
Start: 15:00 EST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Recording ID: f2d9b6a4
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Samantha Patel (Orion - Head InfoSec), Jon Ruiz (Orion - Cloud Architect), Aisha Noor (Orion - Procurement), Dr. Eric Lowe (Orion - Compliance)

Summary:
Quick SIG/CAIQ walkthrough focusing on evidence requests. Customer wants clarity on what can be handed over (SOC 2 report, pen test), what needs redaction, and what we can provide as architecture snaps for private/VPC deployment. Discussed KMS/HSM, key rotation, audit logs retention, RBAC/SCIM SSO, and data residency options (US-only region). Agreed next steps for Redwood to upload signed SIG spreadsheet and evidence bundle.

Topics covered:
- SIG/CAIQ approach and how Redwood maps controls to evidence
- SOC 2 Type II and pen test artifacts availability
- KMS integration, customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) vs Redwood-managed
- Audit log retention windows and how to export logs
- RBAC, SSO (SAML/SCIM) and admin separation for Dedicated/Private
- Data residency / VPC/on-prem considerations and what evidence we can show

Action items (captured above): see separate metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll let people say hi quick. We have Diego and Priya from the Redwood security/SE side and then the Orion team. Quick agenda: walk the SIG, flag any gating evidence, and outline timeline.
[00:12] Samantha Patel: Hi, thanks. We're mainly looking to get a workable evidence bundle so our vendor assurance team can sign off. We have a handful of controls where we need screenshots or policies, not just a yes/no.
[00:22] Jon Ruiz: And also, we want to understand the KMS setup — can we bring our own key or do keys live with Redwood? That impacts our infosec sign-off.
[00:29] Diego Ramos: Great — we'll cover both patterns. Quick note: our transcript generator sometimes swaps words, so if something sounds odd shout out.
[00:36] Aisha Noor: Also procurement needs to know about contract/data residency clauses — US-only hosting in our contract.
[00:43] Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick housekeeping: I'll share a link to the SIG Excel and our evidence bucket after the call. Diego, can you open with SOC 2 and the evidence types?
[00:52] Diego Ramos: Sure. Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering security and availability. We can provide the full report under an NDA. For some items we give redacted artifacts — for example, we can provide redacted AWS config screenshots, KMS key policy snippets, and our pen-test executive summary. Full pen-test detail sometimes requires a separate MSA addendum — but we generally provide a sanitized version.
[01:22] Dr. Eric Lowe: When you say redacted, can you be explicit — will hostnames be removed, or will there still be anything that points to customer data? We need assurance no PHI is in those screenshots.
[01:34] Priya Singh: Yes — all screenshots and logs provided for evidence are scrubbed to remove any tenant-identifying fields. We have a standard redaction process we can document.
[01:42] Samantha Patel: Okay good. On the SIG spreadsheet, there are a few controls — encryption at rest and key rotation policy specifically. How do you manage rotation and do you support external KMS?
[01:52] Diego Ramos: Two options: Redwood-managed keys in our KMS (we rotate keys on a regular schedule and maintain key lifecycle logs) or customer-managed keys via KMS where the customer provides the key and controls rotation. For private deployments we frequently recommend customer-managed keys. We'll include a short doc explaining the KMS integration flows.
[02:11] Jon Ruiz: If we do customer-managed keys, do we get access to the HSM or is the key material only in our cloud account?
[02:17] Priya Singh: For the BYOK in a VPC/private deployment, key material remains in your KMS/HSM in your cloud account — Redwood's runtime references keys via API, but we do not store plaintext keys. For hosted flows, we offer a bring-your-own-key option backed by a KMS in the region.
[02:34] Samantha Patel: That's encouraging. Next: audit logs. What retention windows and what exports do you offer? We need 12 months of immutable logs for auth events.
[02:45] Diego Ramos: Audit logs are retained 90 days by default in hosted. For Dedicated and Private customers we can extend retention to 12 months or integrate with your SIEM via streaming (we push to S3 or direct syslog). We can provide export scripts and a sample audit log schema. We'll add the schema to the evidence bundle.
[03:05] Jon Ruiz: Is there an immutability guarantee? Our compliance team wants assurance logs can't be altered post-write.
[03:11] Diego Ramos: For dedicated-private deployments you can configure write-once S3 lifecycles and object-lock, or stream into your audit system with retention policies. We'll document recommended configurations.
[03:23] Samantha Patel: Good. RBAC & SSO — we need SCIM provisioning and SAML 2.0. Does Redwood support SCIM for group sync and SAML for SSO? Also want admin separation between who can see logs and who can deploy models.
[03:36] Priya Singh: Yes to both. We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM group sync. RBAC is role-based and you can create custom roles, limit access to model deployments and to audit logs. We'll include a role mapping doc and screenshots of the console RBAC UI.
[03:50] Aisha Noor: Any caveats for the private package? We may need Knox/HSM integrations for some of our on-prem nodes.
[03:57] Diego Ramos: For on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs. There are a few connection patterns depending on network topology — we'll capture the diagrams. Priya, can you flag the places in the SIG where evidence is architecture diagrams?
[04:10] Priya Singh: Yep — controls like CI/CD separation and network boundary controls typically point to diagrams. We'll mark those as "diagram" evidence instead of screenshot.
[04:18] [Speaker 2]: Uh, sorry, could I ask, do you have ISO 27001 certificate?
[04:22] Maya Chen: Quick answer: we're in progress on ISO 27001 and expect certification early next year; current evidence set will reference our existing policies and SOC 2 controls that map to many ISO controls. We'll attach the ISO roadmap doc.
[04:34] Samantha Patel: We capture that as a risk — is that acceptable or will our committee push back?
[04:39] Dr. Eric Lowe: It's usually fine if you have SOC 2 and a clear ISO timeline, but they sometimes want an interim risk acceptance. We'll see.
[04:47] Maya Chen: We'll make the timeline explicit in the evidence bundle.
[04:50] Jon Ruiz: On the SIG spreadsheet itself — a couple of Qs about question phrasing. Sometimes you answer "Yes" but the control expects a policy with proof. Do you propose to write short narrative answers with links to evidence?
[04:59] Diego Ramos: Yes — our standard approach is to answer succinctly with a short narrative: e.g., "Yes — Redwood rotates keys every 90 days (see KMS rotation policy, evidence 3)." Then we link to the artifact. We'll deliver the Excel with the answer column and an evidence link column.
[05:16] Samantha Patel: Great. Procurement question: what redaction process will you use for logs that we can't expose? Need confirmation in writing.
[05:24] Priya Singh: We'll include a redaction policy PDF. Essentially, tenant IDs, IPs, and anything that could be PHI is redacted. We can provide hashes for correlation if needed.
[05:33] Aisha Noor: Also need to capture SLAs for evidence requests — how fast can you produce artifacts? Our RFP expects 10 business days for most standard artifacts.
[05:42] Maya Chen: Practically, for SOC 2 and standard artifacts we can meet 10 business days. For pen-test raw data or custom architecture diagrams it might be 15-20 days. We'll itemize per artifact in the upload notes.
[05:54] Jon Ruiz: Regarding network diagrams — can you provide the diagram at high-level for hosted and a separate diagram for private/VPC with peering and egress points? We need to show traffic flows for PHI.
[06:05] Diego Ramos: Yes. We'll provide both: hosted high-level with redacted cloud account IDs and a private deployment diagram that includes VPC peering, NATs, and where KMS calls occur.
[06:16] Samantha Patel: One item on data residency — we require data to stay in US-only region. Is that supported?
[06:21] Priya Singh: Yes — Redwood supports region pinning for hosted, and Dedicated/Private deployments can be deployed into your requested region or on-prem. We'll note which artifacts show region constraints.
[06:31] Dr. Eric Lowe: Do you do subprocessor lists and notify customers of changes?
[06:36] Maya Chen: We maintain a subprocessor list and provide notifications for changes; we'll include the current list and a process doc for notifications.
[06:43] Samantha Patel: A few SIG-specific calls-out: CAIQ question A1 is about external audit of controls, A2 on vulnerability management evidence, and B3 on encryption. We'll need either a screenshot or a policy.
[06:56] Diego Ramos: Understood — for vulnerability management we'll attach our vuln management policy, PR triage workflow, and the pen test executive summary. For patching cadence we'll include a spreadsheet showing patch windows and time-to-remediation SLAs.
[07:11] Jon Ruiz: On proof for encryption in transit — do you publish TLS config and cipher suites?
[07:16] Priya Singh: Yes — we'll include TLS config docs and a TLS scan report. For any custom deployments we can produce a config snippet.
[07:24] [00:07:30] Samantha Patel: (inaudible) — can you also show evidence of separation of duties in your provisioning?
[07:33] Diego Ramos: We'll include an RBAC mapping table and an audit log extract that shows role changes (redacted).
[07:41] Maya Chen: At this point let's talk timeline. Our proposal is: Redwood uploads completed SIG (answers + evidence links) by 2025-12-19. Customer reviews and flags top 12 gating items by 2025-12-22. Follow up on open items week of 2025-12-29. Sound OK?
[07:58] Samantha Patel: Yes that's workable. One more procurement note: will evidence live in a shared S3 bucket or a secure portal? We need download control and access logs.
[08:08] Priya Singh: We'll place artifacts in a temporary secure S3 bucket with time-limited links, or we can host them in a secure portal with audit logs. We'll enable object access logs for all evidence.
[08:20] Aisha Noor: That helps. For legal we may need CDA/NDA before receiving some artifacts.
[08:25] Maya Chen: Noted — we'll send the standard NDA and also flag any artifacts that require an NDA before release.
[08:31] [00:08:40] Jon Ruiz: A quick technical question about KV cache references in your docs — sometimes it's written "KV cache" other times the transcript autocorrects to "K V cash". We just want clarity on caching and whether prefix caching could leak context between tenants.
[08:45] Diego Ramos: No cross-tenant leakage. Prefix caching is tenant-isolated, and we shard caches by customer ID and model variant. We'll add a short note and a code snippet showing tenant isolation.
[08:58] Samantha Patel: Anything else on the SIG?
[09:02] Priya Singh: A few low-level items: we have encryption key rotation logs, MFA enforcement across all admin accounts, and penetration testing cadence annually. We'll show evidence for each.
[09:12] Maya Chen: Great. Let's capture any open questions now so I can add them to the follow-up.
[09:17] Dr. Eric Lowe: Could you confirm whether logs for model inference contain any PII or PHI by default? If they do, what fields are redacted?
[09:26] Diego Ramos: By default inference logs do not capture input text unless you enable logging for debugging — logging is opt-in per customer. When enabled we redact PII/PHI fields and we provide a redaction policy describing the fields we sanitize. We'll include examples.
[09:42] Samantha Patel: That's critical — please include the opt-in toggle UI screenshot.
[09:46] Priya Singh: Will do.
[09:48] Maya Chen: Ok to recap next steps quickly — we'll upload: SIG Excel with narrative answers, evidence bundle (SOC 2, pen-test exec summary, KMS config screenshots, TLS scan, RBAC mapping, architecture diagrams), redaction policy, and the NDA template for items requiring NDA. Upload date 2025-12-19. Customer returns gating list by 2025-12-22. Follow-up call week of 2025-12-29.
[10:10] Aisha Noor: Sounds good. One last procurement ask — list the estimated time to produce non-standard artifacts (like full pen-test raw data).
[10:18] Diego Ramos: Full raw pen-test output typically 20 business days and may require a written request with scope. Executive summary and sanitized output we can provide within the initial 10 business days.
[10:28] Samantha Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll wait for the upload.
[10:32] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll circulate notes and links after the call.
[10:36] [End of recording]
